name: Dynamic Services & Security Limited
sector: Manpower services and trading; battery manufacturing and investment/property exposures
summary: Dynamic is a rapidly expanding manpower and trading operator with battery, Mehai and property exposures, not a simple security-services pure play. FY2026 consolidated revenue is ₹490.92 crore, but owner profit is ₹43.17 crore rather than the ₹46.81 crore group total used in the EPS note. Cash conversion is weak: parent three-year CFO is negative despite ₹48.89 crore cumulative PAT. The low observed ₹122 price does not settle value because economic ownership, newly acquired mall obligations and financing must be modeled separately. Full conditional annual models are provided; BQS and GQS reflect supported factors, while IAS is NS for material claim and funding uncertainty. No verified fraud/default conclusion is implied. [S1][S8][S15][S17][S19]
identity_note: NSE Emerge listing and current 23,518,192 shares cross-checked against annual capital and traded SM master.

score_note: Canonical scores supported by primary history and factor evidence; persistent CASH caps GQS at 5. IAS NS for material economic-claim and financing uncertainties, with conditional full models supplied.

GOV.reason: Promoter-controlled financing and broad related assistance powers require safeguards. Historical predecessor dispute is qualified by issuer response and unknown current closure, not treated as a current fraud finding. Ownership and EPS disclosures need clarification; a small listing fine alone is not a governance failure.

MOAT.reason: Tender capability, operating history and battery qualification support access, but low differentiation, competitive tenders and limited evidence of durable pricing power constrain advantage. No verified market-share moat.

REV.reason: Parent FY2021–26 reported CAGR exceeds 30 percent and recent manpower growth is substantial; parent accounts explain roughly three quarters of latest group revenue increase. Starting band 9 adjusted down one for COVID/proprietorship and goods/services mix distortion. Acquired-period battery comparator is replaced by its actual full-year accounts; this is not a claim of fully organic group growth.

DUR.reason: Recurring manpower needs and railway battery demand offer runway, but tender renewals, customer budgets, funding and unrelated property/solar expansion limit visibility. Award headlines are not an audited remaining backlog.

CAP.reason: Group core EBIT near 76.57 crore against roughly 583.70 crore closing equity plus debt less free cash is about 13 percent pre-tax, not proof of sustained high incremental returns. Parent investments, advances and leveraged new property acquisition require explicit economic claims and deployment evidence.

CASH.reason: Three-year parent CFO is negative despite 48.89 crore profit; group CFO is also negative cumulatively. Capital releases in CFO do not improve underlying realization. Battery standalone CFO is negative despite profit and rapid growth. Persistent weakness, not capex being deducted twice.

BAL.reason: Low free cash, 233.59 crore consolidated debt, mostly current, and additional mall obligations create substantial refinancing exposure. Restricted/escrow balances are not available liquidity. No verified default or insolvency is asserted.

EXEC.reason: Core and battery growth are real, but cash realization, diversified acquisitions, inconsistent scope disclosures and funding discipline remain unproven. Appointments and small new orders do not resolve these.

EARN.reason: Current parent other income is modest, but FY2023 profits contained material other income and current consolidated owner attribution/scope needs reconciliation. Recurring parent cash earnings are weaker than headline profit growth.

R.reason: Conditional base IRR is computable, but material uncertain ownership/control bridge, mall closing claims, recovery and finance availability prevent a supported return point score.

D.reason: Severe and bear scenarios expose potential equity loss and substantial funding needs, but missing mall closing balance and cross-entity claims prevent a calibrated permanent-loss assessment.

P.reason: Low reported P/E is not a sufficient expectations measure with uncertain attributable economic claims and reinvestment funding; reverse hurdles are explicit conditional algebra.

L.reason: Observed-only 60-session median implies 9.83 days at 5 percent participation, but conditional zero fill implies 11.12 days; latest 20-session observation and conditional sensitivities imply 19.37–26.38 days. Downgraded for deterioration, two-trade latest quote, 12.2 percent reference-position lot, fewer than 100 PANs and expired mandatory market making. This is not an executable-price certification.

gates.reason: Promoter-related finance and broad assistance powers require safeguards; predecessor dispute retains issuer response and unknown current closure, not a current fraud finding.
Owner EPS and Mehai control/scope need reconciliation; actual cash bridges reconcile and subsidiary primary accounts permit bounded economic analysis. No blanket failure from small errors.
Parent/battery working capital and mall obligations require substantial modeled finance; proposed FPO and rating limits are not committed cash.
Stale two-trade quote, large reference-position lot and concentrated/declining activity; no claim of suspended trading or guaranteed execution.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of October 20, 2026. Dynamic Services & Security Limited, ISIN INE0DZ701010, NSE SME symbol DYNAMIC. The latest observed official quote is October 16 at ₹122, not a claimed October 19 trade. Current shares are 23,518,192; lot 500. The annual report confirms NSE Emerge listing and current capital; October 2021 listing history predates the entire liquidity window. Archetype: manpower contractor with trading, manufacturing and holding-company exposures. Ind AS parent and consolidated scopes are kept separate. G1 Integrity, G2 Reliability, G3 Funding and G4 Tradability are Conditional. Reviewed material disclosures warrant safeguards, but neither an old allegation nor a ₹1.2 lakh listing fine alone establishes a failed gate. Overall valuation confidence is low; verified historical statements and market observations are higher confidence. [S1][S6][S18][S19][S20]

sections.title: Scorecard & Factor Audit
sections.text: Canonical BQS is 4.10; GQS is 5.00, capped at 5 for persistent CASH weakness. IAS is NS, with available-factor bounds rather than renormalization. GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 4 and EARN 4 are evidence-linked judgments. L is 2 conditional on the ₹5 lakh reference position, not a recommended position size. R, D and P remain NS for specific economic-claim and funding gaps, not merely unspecified scenario probabilities. REV uses the long parent history and full-year subsidiary comparators, with a one-point distortion adjustment; headline consolidated acquisition growth is not called organic growth. The complete factor, weight, cap and confidence audit accompanies the record. [S1][S2][S6][S17][S19]

sections.title: Business Model & Industry Position
sections.text: FY2026 parent revenue comprises ₹248.47 crore manpower/cleaning, ₹56.29 crore goods and ₹10.12 crore solar construction. Labour mobilization, tender qualification, contract execution and receivable collection are central economics; supplier and wage funding precede some client receipts. Group scope adds Mehai operations and Bharat Battery, while the April 2026 mall deal adds a different rental/lease business. Mehai is not simply wholly owned operating cash: June shares verify a 36.45 percent economic stake. Bharat sells lead-acid batteries to railway and other industrial customers; its own FY2026 revenue was ₹51.59 crore. SIS is a larger security/facility/cash-logistics comparator, Krystal competes in government healthcare housekeeping/security, and post-demerger Quess is an adjacent staffing comparator, not its former broad facilities group. Different business mixes preclude blindly importing their multiples. [S1][S7][S8][S15][S16][S17][S22][S23][S24]

sections.title: Moat & Competitive Advantage
sections.text: Long operating history from the proprietor businesses, tender credentials and ability to organize staff help win work. They do not establish persistent pricing power: the primary rating describes fragmented competition and low differentiation. Government and railway customers improve counterparty visibility but can impose price, documentation, payment and renewal risk. Battery qualifications and delivery records provide a different barrier, yet current source review does not establish proprietary technology or a quantified sustainable cost advantage. Recent hospital, sand-services and battery awards show activity, not an independently reconciled backlog or customer-retention moat. No current market-share ranking, top-customer percentage or supplier concentration metric is invented where unavailable. [S6][S7][S17][S23][S26][S27]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Earnings Quality
sections.text: Parent revenue progressed from ₹70.04 crore in FY2021 to ₹71.51, ₹73.12, ₹104.44, ₹153.02 and ₹314.88 crore through FY2026. This supports high reported growth, but the IPO combined predecessor businesses and COVID depressed early activity; tiny pre-transfer company numbers are not a valid starting base. FY2023 parent other income of ₹9.59 crore materially supported ₹9.68 crore PAT. By FY2026 parent other income was ₹1.22 crore and core EBITDA calculates to ₹46.55 crore, about 14.8 percent of sales. Consolidated revenue rose 78.69 percent, but battery FY2025 group contribution of ₹4.82 crore was partial-period. Its own full-year comparator was ₹20.81 crore, making FY2026 growth about 148 percent, still strong but not the headline acquisition multiple. Mehai own revenue increased only about 4 percent to ₹124.45 crore. Parent growth explains roughly 75 percent of group revenue increase, supporting high REV without claiming fully organic group growth. Owner PAT, not all NCI profit, belongs to Dynamic shareholders; the EPS note and control bridge require clarification. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S6][S15][S17]

sections.title: Runway, Reinvestment & Capital Allocation
sections.text: Recurring outsourced services and battery replacement demand provide opportunity, but cash realization must finance it. Parent capital is also tied to ₹105.64 crore investments, ₹32.68 crore restricted deposits and material operating advances. The mall SPA specifies ₹64 crore enterprise value, ₹5.09 crore share consideration and ₹9.91 crore liability repayment, totaling ₹15 crore cash; ₹49 crore obligations remain if all assumed liabilities are treated as debt. The 30-year lease and management rent claim of ₹0.75 crore per month are not independent occupancy or collection evidence. The July FPO ceiling is 4,070,500 shares, with no verified completed priced issuance. May approvals concern existing conversion shares, not additional cash. AGM authority for related assistance and possible battery dilution is not actual deployment. Solar investment recovery is explicitly stressed rather than assigning profits to ambitious capacity announcements. Acquisition returns must exceed the cost of financing and any dilution, not merely enlarge revenue. [S1][S8][S9][S10][S11][S17]

sections.title: Governance & Minority Shareholder Protection
sections.text: Promoters held 59.83 percent at March 31; the dated shareholding filing declares no promoter pledge, NDU or other encumbrance, not perpetual clearance. Related-party exposure includes around ₹30 crore family/director loans and family remuneration/rent. Section 185 and 186 authorizations permit sizeable future assistance but do not demonstrate transfers or diversion. Mehai directors/AOC-1 and ownership notes conflict on associate/subsidiary presentation; its own report still calls Dynamic a holding company, so ownership below 50 percent alone is not proof of incorrect control accounting. Small late-listing fines are economically immaterial by themselves. S.K. Basu was appointed auditor for FY2027–31; no adverse resignation reason is inferred. Pranay Mishra’s October departure cites professional commitments and no other material reason; duplicate filings are one event. The September 2021 IPO prospectus disclosed that West Central Railway terminated a ₹14.73 crore contract of the predecessor proprietorship, M/s. Dynamic Services, forfeited a ₹1.47 crore performance guarantee and debarred that firm under applicable rules, following an allegation about tender financial statements. The same prospectus records the proprietor’s challenge in WP-27892-2019, a February 24, 2020 court decision quashing the impugned order, and the railway’s March 16, 2020 reaffirmation. This is an account of the issuer’s historical disclosure, not an independent finding of misstatement or a claim that the listed company is currently banned by all Railways. Current legal closure and the applicable period were not established in this review. [S1][S6][S12][S13][S14][S15][S16][S18]

sections.title: Financial Forensics & Cash Conversion
sections.text: Parent FY2024–26 CFO of −₹12.68, ₹5.23 and ₹1.94 crore totals −₹5.51 crore against ₹48.89 crore PAT. Group CFO of −₹34.69, ₹20.72 and ₹2.12 crore is also negative cumulatively. FY2026 group cash bridges from ₹0.7405 to ₹4.8685 crore through CFO ₹2.1248, investing −₹173.4045 and financing ₹175.4077 crore: no missing cash is asserted. The ₹112.86 crore investing line labeled PPE includes broader capital movements, not only ₹18.51 crore gross PPE additions. CFO contains noncurrent-asset releases, including a ₹5.18 crore amount matching CWIP reduction; normalization requires a capital/operating bridge. FY2023 CFO differences partly reflect reclassification of short borrowing, not necessarily changed economics. Current group debt is ₹233.59 crore; ₹62.45 crore other bank balances include restricted deposits and ₹29.76 crore escrow, while noncurrent deposits add ₹6.45 crore. Receivables of ₹180.01 crore are presented under six months without ECL, but this does not prove timely collection. Parent other operating assets and group capital/financial advances require counterparty recovery evidence. Bharat’s own CFO is −₹4.98 crore, despite ₹11.03 crore PAT and release of legacy noncurrent assets. Its full-year FY2025 history resolves acquisition-base distortion. Audit opinions are unmodified; the boilerplate going-concern reference is not treated as a located qualified opinion. ₹4.49 crore contested income-tax demand is stressed separately; historical IPO claims are not automatically added to it. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S6][S17]

sections.title: Valuation & Scenario Returns
sections.text: The dated ₹122 quote implies market capitalization of about ₹286.92 crore and approximately 6.65 times FY2026 owner profit on current shares, not 6.13 times total group profit. This is not a normalized fair-value conclusion. The linked five-year model uses actual parent and battery opening cash/debt/WC, half-year draw interest, current tax plus opening-tax settlement, maintenance/completion capex and once-only impairment replacement funding. Parent and battery operating equity, conditional mall equity and attributable Mehai owner-PAT equity are summed without adding investment cost again. Base parent growth/margin/WC assumptions are 12/14/54 percent, battery 12/25/80 percent; exit EBITDA multiples are 8 times. Mall assumes 5 percent rent growth, 75 percent margin and a 10 times exit, with unknown opening cash/WC explicitly unresolved. Mehai uses verified 36.45 percent economics, no cash dividends and explicit pro-rata capital-call sensitivities; this equity module is not a reconstructed target operating forecast. Results are bear: terminal ₹0.00, five-year IRR -100.00%, parent peak debt ₹277.91 crore; base: terminal ₹300.47, five-year IRR 19.75%, parent peak debt ₹200.07 crore; bull: terminal ₹688.44, five-year IRR 41.35%, parent peak debt ₹166.83 crore. Bear and severe outcomes can exhaust equity; these are illustrative stresses, not verified probability bounds. Additional sensitivities pair working capital, target funding gaps, capital calls, battery secondary-sale cash/ownership and FPO cash/shares. A 15 percent analyst hurdle is a convention, not a promise. Specific unverified closing claims, control mapping and funding capacity keep R/D/P and IAS NS despite computable scenarios. [S1][S8][S9][S15][S16][S17][S19] Opening-claim review, 20 October 2026: ₹1.228 crore parent accrued FD interest is now separately included at the conditional terminal deposit-recovery fraction, with a zero-recovery case. It is distinct from FD principal and is not new annual interest income or spendable opening cash. Parent employee/statutory balances and battery current and noncurrent other/CSR payables were already included in net working capital, including the disclosed CSR cheque-clearance balance. No second settlement was added. Target opening accounts, control mapping and financeability remain unresolved; IAS stays NS.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Map
sections.text: Permanent loss can arise without an accounting fraud: growth requiring receivable/security-deposit funding, compressed tender margins, higher borrowing cost, restricted funds that cannot be upstreamed, or a property acquisition earning less rent than debt service. The bear model requires parent peak debt of about ₹277.91 crore and produces no residual combined equity under its assumptions. Severe stress adds a 15 percent noncash impairment of opening parent/battery WC with replacement funding once, the ₹4.49 crore disputed-tax cash payment and a ₹10 crore unknown mall-opening funding stress. New debt is modeled as a requirement, never an approved line. Subsidiary lenders and minority owners rank ahead of freely assumed transfers to parent shareholders. A later FPO can provide funds but dilutes existing shareholders; matched cash/share sensitivities show the trade-off. None of these stress amounts is a verified upper limit or prediction of default. [S1][S8][S9][S15][S17]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold terminal prices from ₹122 are ₹610 and ₹1,220, requiring annualized shareholder returns of 37.97 and 58.49 percent over five years. Holding all other base assumptions fixed, the linked model requires parent revenue CAGR of 38.02 and 63.20 percent respectively, with modeled parent peak debt near ₹616.84 and ₹1499.05 crore. These are algebraic hurdles, not demonstrated financing capacity or probabilities. The bull scenario exceeds fivefold only when faster growth, stronger margin, better cash conversion and higher exit valuation jointly hold. Revenue expansion or an exciting solar/property announcement alone cannot establish a tenfold shareholder outcome. [S1][S8][S9][S19]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require the next balance sheet and receivable/advance collection evidence, a reconciled owner-profit/EPS and Mehai control/ownership bridge, and a cash-versus-capital classification bridge. Obtain mall completion accounts, debt terms, security, actual rents/occupancy and lease obligations before assigning a supported combined valuation. Track actual FPO price, costs, receipt and allotment together; distinguish authority for battery dilution or related assistance from execution. Test core and battery cash conversion separately, and reconcile intercompany claims and any dividends. Update the historical railway dispute only from reliable legal/issuer status evidence, preserving the predecessor and procedural distinctions. Before any implementation, verify live spread, bid depth, lot, surveillance and current encumbrances. Failure of collections, rising short-term leverage or unexplained related deployments would weaken the thesis; small fines or corrected comparatives alone do not establish economic impairment. [S1][S6][S8][S9][S15][S17][S18][S21]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Financing-dependent diversified growth watchlist, not a verified compounder or a price-only value conclusion. Supported operating growth earns credit, but cash conversion, capital allocation and tradability materially constrain quality. The complete conditional model is useful for identifying required claims and financing, not for overriding missing evidence with a precise buy price. G1–G4 remain Conditional, not unsupported fail declarations; IAS remains NS for the specific combined valuation inputs described. This research does not instruct a transaction or determine a suitable position size. [S1][S8][S15][S17][S19]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Review covers the final IPO prospectus, FY2022–26 annual history, original versus recast cash-flow comparisons, issuer and subsidiary audited accounts, shareholding, rating, April acquisition, FPO/voting, past conversion approvals, AGM/auditor and October resignation/order filings. The issuer subsidiary archive and targeted searches did not locate a mall closing balance sheet or independent current closure of the predecessor railway matter. Mehai own FY2026 report and June shareholding were checked to avoid assuming stale economic ownership. Peer sources support business comparison, not unverified P/E rankings. The undated CSV snapshot is not treated as an official quote. Remaining gaps are explicit: current cash/claims, intercompany reconciliation, scope/control, mall opening debt/WC/rents and available finance. They do not negate every historical figure, but prevent a supported combined point valuation. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S8][S15][S16][S17][S22][S23][S24][S25][S28]

methodology: Actual March 2026 standalone balances anchor parent and battery. Restricted deposits are not spendable opening cash. Forecast ratios are not applied backward. Tax payable is paid once separately from current-year tax.

All parent issued shares are preserved. FPO is authorized, not completed: base has no FPO receipt. Sensitivities pair fresh shares with issue-price cash less 3 percent assumed expenses. No price is a management forecast.

Mall acquisition cash 15 comprises 5.09 shares and 9.91 liability repayment; the initial 0.2555 is included, not added. Remaining 49 of the original 58.91 obligations is conservatively treated as interest-bearing. It is not also deducted from parent cash. The unknown target opening cash and WC remain null, with 0/5/10 crore illustrative funding stress, not verified bounds.

Mall rent 9 annually is management-stated, not independently verified collections. Margins, renewal, tax depreciation, occupancy and terminal multiple are assumptions. Five-year exit is within the disclosed 30-year lease, not a perpetual ownership claim.

Interest solves average opening/closing debt circularly. Additional debt is a required funding amount, not committed headroom. Subsidiary borrowings remain at subsidiary level. No automatic fungibility of subsidiary or escrow cash is assumed.

Battery retained direct legal stake uses 50575/50625 shares; the 50-share promoter nominee beneficial ownership is not assumed without documentation. A 25-percentage-point secondary sale pairs parent cash with reduced future claim. It is hypothetical, not the AGM authorization being treated as completion.

Mehai uses independently verified 272895472/748620000 economic ownership, rather than the inconsistent 53.13 percent note. Below 50 percent ownership does not automatically remove accounting control. Its owner PAT excludes its own NCI. Equity multiples do not require a second debt subtraction. Pro-rata capital calls assume other owners participate; failure is an unresolved funding/dilution risk.

Mehai owner-PAT scenarios are conditional equity-claim sensitivities, not a reconstructed operating cash-flow forecast. Its conflicting control/consolidation scope, material asset classification and capital deployment prevent a combined supported point value. This limitation is not cured by assigning probabilities.

Parent investments at cost 105.6379 are NOT added again when battery, Mehai and Solar are valued separately. Already-paid PPE, CWIP and capital advances are not repurchased. Commissioning only moves existing paid capital into the depreciation base. No second terminal addition of operating PPE/WC.

Opening-claim audit 20 October 2026: parent accrued FD interest 1.228 crore is distinct from 32.6843 crore FD principal, outside operating WC and spendable opening cash. Conditional terminal recovery uses the deposit recovery fraction, with a zero-interest-recovery sensitivity. No new annual interest income is invented. Parent gratuity/statutory/employee/customer advances are already in net WC. Battery current other/statutory payables and 0.4056 crore noncurrent other/CSR payables are in net WC once; the CSR cheque-clearance note does not justify paying the same balance again.

Battery long-term advances, government balances and silver totaling 8.0914 are fixed legacy claims with conditional recovery, not immediate funding. Their collection and any intercompany reconciliation remain uncertain. Parent unidentified other operating assets remain in actual WC and are stressed rather than silently written off.

Noncash WC impairment reduces usable opening assets, is added back to CFO and replacement investment is funded once. It is not an extra cash write-off payment. Severe tax cash stress is independent of impairment. Dividends are zero; no automatic upstream transfer finances the parent.
